stories.title: As global drug giants grow cautious, can Chinese biotech keep cashing in on out-licensing?
stories.summary: Record-breaking cross-border deals helped make some formerly loss-making Chinese biotech companies profitable in the first half of the year, but multinational drugmakers are now signalling plans to tighten deal budgets. stories.title: U.S. Amb. Steel meets Japanese envoy, stresses continued trilateral cooperation
stories.summary: U.S. Ambassador to South Korea Michelle Steel has met with her Japanese counterpart and stressed the importance of continued three-way cooperation among Seoul, Washington and Tokyo, the U.S. envoy's social media post showed Tuesday. In her post on X uploaded the previous day, Steel said she had "a thoughtful conversation with Japanese Ambassador Mizushima Koichi on the opportunities ahead" for trilateral cooperation among the United States, South Korea and Japan. "Continued coordination among our three countries will help advance our shared vision for a peaceful, secure, and prosperous Indo-Pacific," she added. It marked the first time Steel has publicly disclosed meetings with other ambassadors to South Korea since taking office last month. Steel also disclosed separate meetings with Canadian Ambassador to South Korea Philippe Lafortune and Israeli Ambassador to South Korea Rafael Harpaz. "It was a pleasure meeting with Ambassador Lafortune and discussing our shared priorities in Korea. The U.S. and Canada remain committed to peace and security on the Korean Peninsula," she said in a separate post. On her meeting with the Israeli envoy, the U.S. ambassador said she looked forward to "continuing our dialogue on issues of mutual interest."

stories.title: Songs created by AI banned from Australia's music charts
stories.summary: Songs that are largely or wholly created by AI have been banned from Australia's music charts. From this week, all releases must be "substantially human made" to be eligible. The Australian Recording Industry Association (ARIA) said the new code would help "promote the human nature of artistry". It follows a controversy around a cover of Madonna's Like. A Prayer by Australian DJ Josh Fawaz which recently topped the ARIA dance singles chart and peaked at number 2 on the country's overall chart. The song has become a staple of commercial radio station playlists and been streamed more than 48 million times on Spotify alone. Fawaz later added generative AI credits to the song after a backlash. ARIA said that Australian artists were competing for attention "in the most crowded market in history" and that it was "not interested in promoting or celebrating the success of AI-generated music that does not contain human artistry". Under the new rules, AI assistance can still be used, but humans must have written the song, and have performed the lead vocal and primary instruments. AI can also still be used for mastering songs and, for example, using drum machines and auto tune. Earlier this year a song was banned from Sweden's music charts because it was created by AI. And in July, the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI) said AI guidelines would be rolled out in Latin America, the Middle East, Africa and Southeast Asia for use in their official charts.

stories.title: Coaching staff set for Asian Games baseball team
stories.summary: The coaching staff for the national baseball team competing at next month's Asian Games was announced Tuesday. The Korea Baseball Organization (KBO), which governs the professional game, and the Korea Baseball Softball Association, in charge of amateur baseball, jointly unveiled the six-man staff to work with manager Ryu Ji-hyun. They will try to lead South Korea to its fifth consecutive gold medal, the KBO said. The list includes three former KBO club managers and one collegiate manager. Kang In-kwon will be the bench coach, after serving in the same role for Ryu at the World Baseball Classic (WBC) in March this year. Kang, former manager of the NC Dinos, is currently the quality control coach for another KBO club, Hanwha Eagles. Another former Dinos manager, Lee Dong-wook, will be back as the fielding coach, following an earlier stint in the same role during the WBC. Choi Won-ho will be South Korea's pitching coach, after working as the quality control coach for the WBC team. Choi, one-time Eagles manager, has been in the broadcast booth as a color commentator since last year. KT Wiz quality control coach Park Kyung-su was named the hitting coach for the national team, his first appearance on a national team staff. Kyung Hee University manager Choi Tae-won will join the national team as the strategy coach. Choi previously served on coaching staffs for six KBO clubs.
